peu ſ'en falut, qu'au temps de Cornelius Sylla, ne fiſt
priuer le vray enfant d'Aſſidio, des biens paternels: car
il auoit ſi bien affuſté l'artillerie de ſes ruſes, que le iu-
gement ſ'en eſtoit enſuyui en ſa faueur. mais Auguſte
Ceſar empereur ſage, prudent, & heureux prince, ayant
ſubtilement mis l'impoſture en lumiere, fit rendre le
le bien au fils legitime, & mourir l'affronteur en pri-
ſon {b}. Au meſme temps, en la ville de Milan, vne fem-
me fort opulente, appellée Rubrie: par grand deſaſtre
ſe bruſla: apres la mort de laquelle, comme ſes heritiers
auoient deſia vendu la meilleure partie du bien, vne au
tre femme ſe preſenta, ſoy diſant eſtre Rubrie, deman-
dant que ſon bien luy fuſt rendu: à laquelle pluſieurs
meſmes des ſoldats d'Auguſte aſſiſtoient, perſuadez,
pour la ſimilitude qu'elle auoit, & du viſage & des
meurs, auec la defuncte, que ce fuſt veritablement Ru-
brie. mais l'incomparable prudence de ce renommé
& generenx Empereur, empeſcha l'execution de la
fraude. {c}
Lequel bien, depuis iceluy du Tilh au-
roit vendu à pluſieurs & diuers perſon-
nages.
De ce faict, à l'aduenir pourra naiſtre vne queſtion,
ſi le vray mari ſuruenant, pourra retracter les aliena-
tions de ſon bien, & non ſeulement les piecẽs vendues
mais encore recouurer les fruicts recueillis, & perceus
par les achepteurs depuis le tẽps des contracts. pour la
deciſion duquel doute, faut preſuppoſer, qu'vn chacum
peut librement vendre, non ſeulement ſon bien propre
duquel il eſt maiſtre & ſeigneur: mais auſsi le bien

uncertain.note: the note with key a has no marker printed anywhere in this page's body; the italic 'a' that stands to the right of blocks[0].lines[0] (body-1.jpg x~1700) sits in the margin column, at the same left edge as the key letters b/c/d/e, so it is this note's key and not a body marker. The marker it answers is presumably at the foot of the preceding page (p022). Recorded per §4.

uncertain.text: le bien au fils legitime, & mourir l'affronteur en pri-
uncertain.note: sic: the article 'le' is set twice, once at the end of lines[6] ('fit rendre le') and again at the start of this line. Transcribed as printed, not corrected.

uncertain.text: & generenx Empereur, empeſcha l'execution de la
uncertain.note: sic 'generenx' for 'genereux': the letter before the x is a clear n (two stems joined by an arch, body-4.jpg x~330-380). Transcribed as printed.

uncertain.text: tions de ſon bien, & non ſeulement les piecẽs vendues
uncertain.note: 'piecẽs': a clear wavy tilde sits over the second e of 'pieces' (body-6.jpg x~1230 y~360). Sense wants plain 'pieces'; an acute is excluded (this font's acute is a straight slanted stroke). Transcribed as printed per §2.

uncertain.text: deciſion duquel doute, faut preſuppoſer, qu'vn chacum
uncertain.note: sic 'chacum' for 'chacun': the final letter is an unambiguous m with three stems (body-7.jpg x~1430). Transcribed as printed.

uncertain.text: duquel il eſt maiſtre & ſeigneur: mais auſsi le bien
uncertain.note: 'auſsi' is set with long s followed by round s (ſ + s), not the ſſ ligature used elsewhere on the page; kept as printed per §2.

sic 'an' for 'au': the second letter of the last word has two stems joined by an arch at the top (an n), unlike the 'au' of margin_notes[0].lines[0] and margin_notes[2].lines[0]. Transcribed as printed.

two doubtful sorts in one line (margin-1.jpg y~1075-1135). (1) 'liurc': the last letter is a round open c, not the closed italic e used in 'Valere' just above, so 'liure' is printed with a wrong sort. (2) the single letter between 'ix.' and 'xvi.' has both an ascender and a descender (about 2.5x x-height) and a right-turned top terminal, i.e. an italic long ſ or possibly ç; it is plainly not the round c sort used in margin_notes[0].lines[3] ('c. xvi.'). Sense requires 'c.' (chapitre), matching note a's citation of the same work; read as printed here, but an emendation to 'c.' is defensible.

the last letter before the point is a round e, not the t of 'empt.' in margin_notes[3].lines[2] and margin_notes[4].lines[0] (margin-3.jpg y~985-1020). Sense wants 'empt.' (de actione empti); transcribed as printed.
an acute accent is visible over the final e of 'gué.' (margin-2.jpg y~700-760); the ink is light and the reading of the accent, not of the letters, is what is in doubt.
